title: Isolate generator main 52-GM of path A for maintenance (rack out, stored energy, lockout)
summary: Path A is on utility, 52-GM is open and the generator bus is in standby. Maintenance needs 52-GM out of its cell. At the 13.8 kV switchgear (field view), in the order of OSHA 29 CFR 1910.147(d): take local control, rack 52-GM through TEST to DISCONNECTED (isolation), apply your personal padlock to the racking mechanism (lockout), then relieve the stored energy: close and open 52-GM with its mechanical push buttons until the closing spring reads DISCHARGED (no control power in DISCONNECTED, so the motor cannot recharge it). 52-U carries path A the whole time: touching it ends the drill. Switching the procedure does not call for counts as a violation.
references: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.147(d)(4)(i): lockout devices are affixed to each energy isolating device by authorized employees (verified against the eCFR text, Cornell LII, 2026-11-26)
OSHA 29 CFR 1910.147(d)(5)(i): after the lockout devices are applied, stored or residual energy is relieved, disconnected, restrained or otherwise rendered safe (verified 2026-11-26)
OSHA 29 CFR 1910.147(e)(3): each lockout device is removed by the employee who applied it (verified 2026-11-26)
Mechanical close / trip push buttons on the breaker front without control power: common draw-out breaker practice, verify against the vendor manual

steps.text: Take local control: MV transfer A authority to LOCAL (remote and automatic close blocked)
Rack 52-GM from CONNECTED to TEST (field view, racking crank)
Rack 52-GM to DISCONNECTED (isolated from the bus, no control power)
Apply your personal padlock to the 52-GM racking mechanism
Relieve the stored energy after the lock: close and open 52-GM with its mechanical push buttons until the spring reads DISCHARGED

fail.reason: 52-U opened: wrong breaker, the utility incomer carries path A (load on battery)
86 of 52-U tripped: wrong breaker, path A lost its incomer
